text:
kyle: FYI saw a flake in the GPU-provisioner helm chart during a dry-run — template helper that flattens tolerations is returning an empty list as `null` which makes `range` crash on render in our GitOps pipeline

maria: can you paste the minimal values that trigger it?

kyle: repro snippet: 
```
values.yaml:
provisioner:
  tolerations: []
```
helper:
```
{{- define "pp.tolerations" -}}
{{- $t := .Values.provisioner.tolerations | default nil -}}
{{- range $t }}
- key: gpu
  operator: Exists
{{- end -}}
{{- end -}}
```

kyle: with empty slice we expect no tolerations rendered, but helm template fails with "range of nil" in CI

ashley: hmm, `default nil` is the problem — default should be `list` or empty slice. Try `default (list)` or `default (slice)` depending on chartlib.

samir: in our helper library we usually coerce with `coalesce` helper: `{{- $t := coalesce .Values.provisioner.tolerations (list) -}}` that avoids nil ranges. Also add a quick unit test in helm-unittest for the helper.

leo: another safe pattern: `{{- range $t := .Values.provisioner.tolerations -}}` works but uglier. I'd prefer explicit check: `{{- if .Values.provisioner.tolerations }}{{- range ... }}` to be defensive.

maria: We should also update values schema so `tolerations` type is array by schema and not nullable. That way linter will catch it pre-merge. Add `type: array` and `nullable: false` in values.schema.json for `provisioner.tolerations`

ashley: good call. Do we have a helm chart lint rule in CI that validates values.schema.json?

samir: yes but it only runs `helm lint` which doesn't enforce JSON schema by default. We recently added a small job `helm-values-validate` that runs `conftest` against values.schema.json — but it's flaky unless we pin the exact schema paths. Will open a follow-up.

kyle: for immediate fix I'll push a tiny patch to the helper to coalesce to `(list)`, and add an assertion in the unit test. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/4567 — cc @maria @ashley

ci-bot: Build queued: pipeline #4567. Running helm-lint, helm-unittest, gitops-dry-run.

ashley: also note this surfaced only on k8s cluster in eu-west-3 because our GitOps operator has `--strict` rendering in that cluster (different helm binary flags). So region constraints triggered the pipeline failure not the chart itself. Document that nuance in the PR description.

maria: ack. can we add a small note in CHARTS.md about required shape for tolerations to avoid future confusion?

samir: yes and add a quick healthcheck in the GitOps template that fails fast if a required array is null. Minimal check: `{{- if not (kindIs "slice" .Values.provisioner.tolerations) }}{{ fail "tolerations must be an array" }}{{- end }}` — but `fail` will break local `helm template` so gate it behind `{{- if .Capabilities.KubeVersion.GitVersion }}` or better, only in CI.

leo: can we add a linter rule in pre-commit that runs `helm template` with `--strict`? small cost but catches these env-drift issues early.

kyle: sounds good. PR updated with helper change, unit test, values.schema.json change, and PR description documenting eu-west-3 strictness. link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/4567

ci-bot: pipeline #4567 succeeded: helm-lint ✅, helm-unittest ✅, gitops-dry-run ✅.

maria: great — thanks for the quick fix. I'll follow up to add schema validation job to CI and a pre-commit hook for strict-mode linting.

ashley: thanks, dropping a :thumbsup: in the PR.

kyle: thanks everyone, marking thread resolved and adding a retro note to infra-ops for pattern of array coersion.
